item.title: Fall Migration at Cape May — Mon Sep 14, 7:00 AM — NJ
item.description: Join Louise Zemaitis for this three-day birding workshop exploring Cape May’s September bird migration! September straddles the migratory timetable – not too late for shorebirds, not too early for hawks, and right on time for Neotropical songbird migrants. Our time will largely be spent getting to know the great wealth of warblers, flycatchers, vireos and other migratory songbirds that pause at Cape May during their southward migration at this time of year. This migration is very much weather-dependent, so there are no guarantees on what we may see, but it is pretty certain that each day will be very different to the last, creating a wonderful atmosphere of intrigue and an element of the unknown. While songbirds will be a major focus for us, we shall also spend time sampling the shorebirds, seabirds and raptors that also pass through at this time. item.title: Eagle Rock Reservation — Fri Oct 2, 9:15 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.
We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.
Will will meet at: [https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1
If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.
Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

item.title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series — Mon Oct 12, 5:30 PM — Cole Hall 141
item.description:

This 10-week workshop series offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala and are open to students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University. No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. item.title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday — Sun Oct 18, 9:00 AM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.
Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.
Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

item.title: Watchung Booksellers Hosts Bestselling Author Amanda Peters — Mon Sep 14, 7:00 PM — watchung booksellers the kids’ room
item.description:
Watchung Booksellers welcomes Amanda Peters, bestselling author of The Berry Pickers, for the release of her latest novel, The Birthing Tree, on Monday, Sept 14 at 7:00 p.m. Peters will be in conversation about the book with author Alice Elliott Dark. The Birthing Tree is an unforgettable novel about a woman who must confront her family’s buried truths and memories of passionate young love when her grandmother’s death leaves her as the only guide to her community’s future. Spanning decades of loss and reclamation, this sweeping yet intimate novel follows one woman’s journey to protect the land, the traditions, and the memory of the women who came before her—and to decide which parts of her inheritance she will carry into the future. Tickets are $5 and include a 10% discount on the book purchased at the event. To register, visit watchungbooksellers.com. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook
